title: Set local systems: finite subobjects, colimits and finite etale total spaces
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. On its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], call a set sheaf a local system if it is ind-finite etale [def-per-ind-finite-etale-local-system]. A finite local system means a sheaf represented by a finite etale $X$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. (1) Every local system is the filtered union, in ambient set sheaves, of its finite local-system subsheaves. The full category of local systems is closed under all small ambient colimits and finite limits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. (2) Let $q:Y\to X$ be finite etale, with $Y$ Noetherian. The equivalence between set sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ and set sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ equipped with a map to $h_Y$ sends $E$ to its total-space sheaf $q_!E\to h_Y$. In the reverse direction it sends $p:F\to h_Y$ to the sheaf whose sections on $(a:U\to Y)$ are $\{t\in F(U):p(t)=a\}$. It preserves the corresponding group actions, with a $G$-action over $h_Y$ corresponding to a $q^{-1}G$-action on $E$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Pullback $q^{-1}$ preserves local systems, and $q_!$ sends local systems on $Y$ to local systems on $X$. Here $q^{-1}$ is the inverse image on set sheaves, identified for etale $q$ with restriction to $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. Explicitly $(q_!E)(U)=\coprod_{a\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,Y)}E(U,a)$, with restriction along $V\to U$ induced by $a\mapsto a|_V$ and by restriction in $E$; this presheaf is a sheaf. In the action assertion $G$ is a group sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, and the action on $F$ is required to leave $p:F\to h_Y$ fixed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Propositions 7.2.2–7.2.4, pp. 301–302; the finite-subobject union and the slice/total-space equivalence q_! are used explicitly in the proof of Lemma 7.2.6, p. 302. No torsion extension-closure assertion is included.

proof.text: First record the finite-stage calculation. A finite diagram of finite locally constant set sheaves can be trivialized on an etale cover; the local-section description of sheafification lets us refine further so that every arrow is a fixed map between its finite sets (there are only finitely many elements, arrows and objects). Its finite limit is then the constant sheaf of the corresponding finite-set limit: the sheaf equalizer condition verifies this locally. Its finite colimit is the constant sheaf of the finite-set colimit: the constant-presheaf functor preserves colimits objectwise, and sheafification, being a left adjoint, preserves colimits. These calculations descend: for each member $j:U_i\to X$ of the cover, restriction to $U_i$ is the set-valued inverse image $j^{-1}$, which is a left adjoint (to $j_*$) and so carries the ambient colimit on $X$ to the colimit of the restricted diagram on $U_i$, while limits restrict sectionwise; and compatible maps of sheaves glue uniquely. Thus finite limits and finite colimits of finite local systems, computed in all set sheaves, are finite local systems by the finite-etale/FLC equivalence. The same calculation shows that a map of finite local systems with injective fibre at a geometric point on a connected base is an ambient monomorphism: the finite fibre equivalence identifies its kernel pair with the diagonal, and the ambient finite-limit calculation applies.

source.place: XVII 7.2.4, finite-stage part of the stated stability properties; finite-set calculation expanded by Q127.

proof.text: Suppose $X$ connected, choose $x$, and write $F=\varinjlim_i h_{P_i}$. By the set-valued monodromy equivalence, $F_x=\varinjlim_i |(P_i)_x|$ equivariantly. The image of each finite stage is a finite invariant subset, so these images exhaust $F_x$. All finite invariant subsets $A\subseteq F_x$ form a small directed poset under union (including the empty subset). The finite fibre equivalence gives a finite local system $P_A$ for each $A$, compatible with inclusions, and the full set-valued equivalence gives compatible maps $P_A\to F$. The ambient filtered colimit $L=\varinjlim_A P_A$ is a local system by its definition, and its fibre is $\bigcup_A A=F_x$. Hence $L\to F$ is an isomorphism by the equivalence. Each $P_A\to L$ is an ambient monomorphism: transitions are ambient monomorphisms by step 1; evaluation of this filtered colimit on affine etale objects is a set colimit by the affine-site comparison and the affine-section colimit lemma, so these injections stay injective. The affine-site equivalence detects monomorphisms. Consequently the $P_A$ are finite subsheaves of $F$, and every finite local-system subsheaf is among them, since its fibre inclusion determines it by full faithfulness. This proves precisely the filtered-union assertion.

source.place: XVII 7.2.2–7.2.3 and the finite-subsystem union used at the start of 7.2.6.

proof.text: Finite products are obtained by taking products of finite subsystems: $F\times G$ is the ambient filtered colimit of the finite local systems $F_a\times G_b$. Indeed finite limits of sheaves are computed sectionwise, and on the affine etale basis evaluation commutes with filtered colimits; there the assertion is filtered-colimit/finite-product commutation for sets. The terminal sheaf is represented by $X$. For two maps $u,v:F\rightrightarrows G$, their monodromy maps send each finite invariant subset $A\subset F_x$ into a finite invariant subset $B\subset G_x$. Full faithfulness gives the corresponding maps $F_A\rightrightarrows G_B$. Their ambient equalizer $E_{A,B}$ is finite by step 1. Enlarging $A,B$ gives a filtered system. Its colimit is the ambient equalizer of $u,v$: on the affine basis every section of $F$ comes from some $F_A$, and equality of its images in $G$ is witnessed at a sufficiently large finite stage by the set-colimit equivalence relation. This also gives injectivity of the comparison. Products and equalizers supply all finite limits, including the empty limit.

An arbitrary small coproduct of local systems is the filtered colimit of the finite coproducts of their finite subsystems: a map from either candidate to an arbitrary sheaf $H$ amounts exactly to one map from each summand to $H$, by the universal properties of the filtered unions and finite coproducts. Each finite coproduct is finite by step 1, so the ambient coproduct is a local system. This includes the empty coproduct, represented by the empty finite etale cover.

For $u,v:F\rightrightarrows G$, take the directed poset of pairs of finite invariant subsets $(A,B)$ of $(F_x,G_x)$ such that $u(A)\cup v(A)\subseteq B$. These pairs exhaust both fibres, since one can enlarge $B$ by the two finite images. Let $C_{A,B}$ be the ambient coequalizer of the finite-stage pair $F_A\rightrightarrows G_B$; it is a finite local system by step 1. The ambient filtered colimit $C$ of the $C_{A,B}$ is a local system. For every ambient sheaf $H$, compatible maps $C_{A,B}\to H$ amount to compatible maps $G_B\to H$ equalizing $u,v$ on every $F_A$. By the filtered-union assertion this is exactly a map $G\to H$ equalizing $u,v$ on $F$. Thus $C$ is the ambient coequalizer. For a diagram $D:I\to\mathcal L(X)$, its colimit is the coequalizer of the two maps $\coprod_{a:i\to j}D(i)\rightrightarrows\coprod_iD(i)$, one induced by each $D(a)$ and one by source inclusion: maps from this coequalizer to $H$ are exactly cocones on $D$. Both coproducts are small. This proves closure under every small ambient colimit.

source.place: XVII 7.2.4, inductive limits; finite relations and the universal property expanded by Q127.

proof.text: For a general Noetherian $X$, every nonempty set of closed subsets of $|X|$ has a minimal element, so (taking complements) every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes; hence its connected components form a finite open-and-closed partition. A sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the same as a tuple of sheaves on those components: for $U\to X$, write $U$ as the disjoint union of its pullbacks to the components and apply the sheaf gluing condition. Thus ambient limits and colimits are componentwise. A finite tuple of finite etale covers gives a finite etale cover of $X$, and a finite tuple of filtered presentations can be indexed by their filtered product. The connected arguments therefore give all of clause (1). If $X$ is empty, the empty covering forces every sheaf to have exactly one section on the unique empty object; the sole sheaf is represented by the empty cover, so the same conclusions hold.

Let $q:Y\to X$ be finite etale. Objects of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ identify with pairs $(U,a)$, where $U$ is etale over $X$ and $a:U\to Y$ is an $X$-map: composition is etale and cancellation makes every such $a$ etale. Coverings are the same underlying jointly surjective etale families. Define $T(E)(U)=\coprod_{a:U\to Y}E(U,a)$. For matching local sections $(a_i,t_i)$, the labels $a_i$ glue uniquely to $a:U\to Y$ because $h_Y$ is a sheaf (it is finite locally constant by the finite-etale/FLC equivalence). Then the $t_i$ glue uniquely in $E$ over $(U,a)$. Hence $T(E)$ is already a sheaf and has its label map to $h_Y$. Conversely $E_p(U,a)=\{t\in F(U):p(t)=a\}$ is a sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ by the sheaf condition for $F$. The bijection $\coprod_a E_p(U,a)\to F(U)$ forgets the label, whose inverse is $t\mapsto(p(t),t)$. The fibre of $T(E)(U)$ at $a$ is exactly $E(U,a)$. These inverse maps commute with restrictions and all sheaf maps; they prove the claimed equivalence and identify $q_!$ with $T$.

source.place: XVII 7.2.6, p. 302, identification of a sheaf over the finite local system $Y$ with a sheaf on $Y$; explicit construction expanded by Q127.

proof.text: If a group sheaf $G$ acts on $F$ with $p(gt)=p(t)$, then for each $(U,a)$ the formula $(g,t)\mapsto gt$ restricts to $G(U)\times E_p(U,a)\to E_p(U,a)$. Set-valued etale inverse-image/restriction identifies $G(U)$ here with $(q^{-1}G)(U,a)$. Thus these are exactly the sectionwise maps of a $q^{-1}G$-action on $E_p$, with identity and associativity unchanged. Conversely such fibre actions define the action of $G(U)$ on $T(E)(U)$ by $(g,(a,t))\mapsto(a,gt)$. The displayed inverse equivalence preserves equivariant maps. In particular a free action remains free, since for each fixed $t$ the equality $gt=t$ is tested in the same fibre.

source.place: XVII 7.2.6, action of $G$ corresponds to action of $q^*G$ on the associated sheaf.

proof.text: For any ambient sheaf $H$ on $X$, a map $T(E)\to H$ is exactly a family of maps $E(U,a)\to H(U)$ natural on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$. Inverse-image/restriction therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}_X(T(E),H)=\operatorname{Hom}_Y(E,q^{-1}H)$, naturally. Hence $T=q_!$ preserves all small colimits by the left-adjoint lemma. Also $q^{-1}$ preserves colimits by its set-valued adjunction to $q_*$. On finite stages $q^{-1}h_P=h_{P\times_XY}$ directly by restriction and the fibre-product universal property; this is finite etale by base change. On a finite stage $E=h_P$ over $Y$, $T(E)(U)$ is the set of pairs $a:U\to Y$, $b:U\to P$ with $a$ equal to the structure map after $b$, hence is exactly $h_P(U)$ with $P$ now over $X$. The composite $P\to Y\to X$ is finite etale by finite and etale composition. Passing through any filtered finite-stage presentation, both $q^{-1}$ and $q_!$ thus preserve local systems. These formulas also cover empty $Y$ and empty fibres; no surjectivity of $q$ is used.

source.place: XVII 7.2.4 and 7.2.6, finite-etale total spaces and inverse images; adjunction verified on sections.
